input: # divergent.tsv -- the shape of a divergence register, used by this
# package's own tests.
#   input     the source every port is given.
#   ts,go,rs  what each port produces, in the ordinary expected
#             vocabulary: a JSON value, or ERROR:<code>.
# One column per runtime, which is what a register is: three ports means
# three columns. Two of them are not enough to exercise the shape a real
# register has, because a row where THIS port has converged with one
# other and not the rest is reported differently (PARTIALLY closed) from
# one where it has converged with all of them.
# A REAL register lives in the repo whose ports disagree, and every row
# is a divergence someone decided not to repair. This file is a stand-in so
# the mechanism itself can be tested; the fake parser in the tests answers
# these inputs.
# The rule that makes a register different from a fixture: a row must record
# a DISAGREEMENT. Two cells saying the same thing assert nothing and would
# pass forever -- which is how 29 prose divergence claims outlived the
# divergences they described.
a
b
c
